'''Football Club Dinamo Tbilisi''' ({{lang-ka|დინამო თბილისი}}, {{IPA|ka|dinamo tʰbilisi|pron}}) is a [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Tbilisi]] that competes in the [[Erovnuli Liga]], the top flight of Georgian football.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Football Club Dinamo Tbilisi history |url=https://www.footballhistory.org/club/dinamo-tbilisi.html |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=www.footballhistory.org}}</ref>

Dinamo Tbilisi was one of the most prominent clubs in Soviet football and a major contender in the [[Soviet Top League]] almost immediately after it was established in [[1936 Soviet Top League|1936]]. The club was then part of one of the leading sport societies in the [[Soviet Union]], the [[Dynamo Sports Club|All-Union Dynamo sports society]] which had several other divisions besides football and was sponsored by the Soviet Ministry of Internal Affairs. Its main claim to European fame was winning the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] in [[1981 European Cup Winners' Cup Final|1981]], beating [[FC Carl Zeiss Jena]] of [[East Germany]] 2–1 in the final in Düsseldorf.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=McCracken |first=Craig |date=2015-09-07 |title=How Dinamo Tbilisi enthralled British football fans in the midst of the Cold War |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/beyond-the-last-man/2015/sep/07/dinamo-tbilisi-liverpool-west-ham |access-date=2026-03-05 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> It remains the only club based in Georgia to have ever lifted a trophy in European competition. Throughout its history, FC Dinamo Tbilisi produced many famous Soviet players: [[Boris Paichadze]], [[Avtandil Gogoberidze]], [[Shota Iamanidze]], [[Mikheil Meskhi]], [[Slava Metreveli]], [[Murtaz Khurtsilava]], [[Manuchar Machaidze]], [[David Kipiani]], [[Vladimir Gutsaev]], [[Aleksandre Chivadze]], [[Vitaly Daraselia]], [[Ramaz Shengelia]], and [[Tengiz Sulakvelidze]]. After the break-up of the Soviet Union, it would later produce some of the finest Georgian players such as [[Temur Ketsbaia]], [[Shota Arveladze]], [[Georgi Kinkladze|Giorgi Kinkladze]], [[Kakha Kaladze]], [[Levan Kobiashvili]], [[Khvicha Kvaratskhelia]], [[Giorgi Mamardashvili]] etc.<ref name=":0" />

Dinamo Tbilisi was one of a handful of teams in the [[Soviet Top League]] (along with [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]] and [[FC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]]) that were never relegated. Their most famous coach was [[Nodar Akhalkatsi]], who led the team to the Soviet title in [[1978 Soviet Top League|1978]], two [[Soviet Cup]]s ([[1976 Soviet Cup Final|1976]] and [[1979 Soviet Cup Final|1979]]), and the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] in [[1981 European Cup Winners' Cup Final|1981]]. He was also one of three co-coaches of the [[Soviet Union national football team]] during the [[FIFA World Cup]] in [[1982 FIFA World Cup|1982]]. FC Dinamo Tbilisi are also 16–time [[Erovnuli Liga|Georgian league]] champions and 13–time [[Georgian Cup]] holders (the current records).<ref name=":0" />"}}
